messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] MD not HTML
parts:
I think that should be a question for RStudio developers.

The MD file is generated as well, and the problem is only that the
HTML file is shown in the preview. If you want to read the MD file,
you have to open it manually (under the same directory as your Rmd
source). I think you can open it in RStudio, and whenever you Knit
HTML, the MD file in RStudio will be reloaded.

The "MD viewer" you mentioned really sounds like an HTML viewer
instead. An MD viewer can be any software that can open a pure text
file, e.g. Notepad++, gedit, Emacs, ... so perhaps you were asking for
an MD converter.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] MD not HTML
parts:
Even in Marked, there must be some sort of conversion behind the
scene. Markdown itself is just plain text without formatting.

According to http://www.tomtorsneyweir.com/reproducable-research, the
MD file will be automatically updated in Marked if it is modified by
another program, so I think you can still open MD in Marked, but
compile Rmd in RStudio. I do not use Mac, so I'm not completely sure.

messages.author: ca3205004f4bea24
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] MD not HTML
parts:
There is a partial Markdown viewer / editor solution for Github called
"Prose.io". Browse to 'prose.io' and do the Github oauth connection.
As long as everything's on Github, some combination of RStudio server,
a modern browser, Github and prose.io will probably give you a
reasonable workflow.

Personally, I really resent Github's adoption/enhancement of
Github-flavored Markdown for Github Pages, their issues and their
wikis. I think it smacks of programmers imposing their personal
opinions on how software should be made / documented onto other
programmers, rather than listening to users who just want to get shit
done for paying customers and win-win sales closed with new customers.
I've spent a week wrestling with Octopress, and that's probably the
*simplest* interface to Github Pages. Raw Jekyll is *much* worse, and
their automated page generator only has a few fixed styles to work
with.
